comments.author: SkebbZ
comments.body_html: What is “pmcsGearWeightMultiplier” in the config?

comments.author: turbodestroyer
comments.body_html:
In 2.0.0 (SPT 4) it’s actually depricated, on a pair with ‘sellClothingOnRagman’ - I just forgot to remove them.

In 1.4.0 (SPT 3.11) it is PMC-specified multiplier for “weight” option, which is responsible for how often you will see this item on vanilla bots. Eg, let’s consider an Umka vest - if its “weight” is 0.5 and pmcsGearWeightMultiplier is 2, you will see it 0.5 times as often as regular Umka on Scavs, and 0.5*2=1 times often as regular Umka on specified PMCs.

Honestly it was quite confusing option, should have made it hardcoded right away. Not even to mention that probably the most of people use Algorithmic Level Progression or Progressive Bot System mods, and they use their own logic to select gear for bots.

comments.author: turbodestroyer
comments.body_html:
Hey! Sounds cool, thanks for your interest, let me know if you need anything from my end!

As for detecting the mod, keep in mind that it’s possible to disable items in this mod, so just relying on detection most likely isn’t reliable. I’m not sure people actually disable anything, but it’s possible.

It’s probably easier for you as a mod developer to just check whether item you want bots to wear exists in db. Probably filter all your items with something like ItemHelper>IsItemInDb, or (better) with mapping the db ids into a list (that you’d compare your item pool with) at the point where you’re sure all mods are loaded.

comments.author: turbodestroyer
comments.body_html:
Eg in Croupier I map the whole db once, when I’m 100% sure every gear/gun mod is loaded and then exclude items that don’t exist there. There are lots of stuff from now dead mods in the item pool, but it all works fine since everything that is not in db just gets filtered out.

Croupier.cs lines 228-232
